More, Less or Equal

ArithmeticCounting
Game: Change the numbers and see whether the left side is more than, less than or equal to the right.
How to play: Press + or − by a number, or click its right half to go up and its left half to go down. Pick +, −, × or ÷ below.
+
=
Operation
Look for the math

Counting comes first; adding is a quicker way to count, and the signs >, < and = record what a count shows. Here you start from the plain fact 1 + 1 = 2 and change it one step at a time.

Keeping the balance

An equality is like a balance. Put one more thing in either group on the left and the left becomes more: 1 + 2 > 2. To make it equal again, the right side must grow by one too: 1 + 2 = 3. The logic test tried every true sum a + b = c with a and b from −20 to 20 and found this always.

Below zero

Nothing stops a number at zero: keep pressing − and you meet the negative numbers. A negative number in the middle is written in brackets, 3 − (−2) > 1, so the two minus signs do not run together. Taking away a negative number makes the left side bigger.

Dividing, and dividing by zero

For a ÷ b the sign compares the exact fraction a/b with c: 7 ÷ 2 > 3, because 7/2 is three and a half. The applet never divides: it compares a with b × c, and turns the answer round when b is negative. When b = 0 there is no answer at all (division by zero), so the sign becomes ≠. The test compared every equation with all three numbers from −25 to 25 against the applet's own method and against exact arithmetic.

With ×, make a × b = c true, then add one to a. How much must c grow now?
